name: Days Sales Outstanding
summary: Weighted DSO is 69 days versus a 50-day target. The gap is driven mostly by past-due concentration on capital-equipment milestone billing and slow institutional / international payers — not by everyday terms.

drivers.name: Past-due concentration
drivers.narrative: 41% of the $78,353,289 book is past due. Every dollar past terms directly extends DSO.
drivers.rootCause: Capital systems are milestone-billed (order, ship, install, acceptance); acceptance disputes and slow government/EMEA/APAC payers leave large balances 60–90+ days past due.

drivers.name: Contractual payment terms
drivers.narrative: Average institutional terms run NET60–90; distributors and government longer still.
drivers.rootCause: Government (GSA), academic consortia and international distributors negotiate NET60–90 as standard — structurally higher than commercial NET30.

drivers.name: Unapplied cash drag
drivers.narrative: Cash received but not yet applied keeps invoices open and inflates DSO.
drivers.rootCause: Wire payments arrive without remittance detail; manual matching backlog delays clearing — the Cash Application accelerator targets this directly.

drivers.name: Regional / payer mix
drivers.narrative: Past-due exposure is concentrated in slower-paying regions.
drivers.rootCause: EMEA public hospitals and China/JV distributors carry longer effective payment cycles than US cancer centers.
